The evidence is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Act, for each is made easy for that for which he was created." [92] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/82.]]

Thumma amatahu: He takes his soul. Fa-aqbarahu: He makes him such that he is buried and interred. It is said: qabartu al-mayyit, when I buried the dead; and Allah aqbarahu, meaning He made him such that he is buried and made him one with a grave. The Arabs say: batarta dhanab al-baʿir and Allah abtarahu; ʿadabtu qarn al-thawr and Allah aʿdabahu; tardtu fulanan and Allah yatrudahu, meaning He made him an outcast. Al-Farra' said: its meaning is that He made him one who is buried, and did not make him one who is cast to beasts and birds, nor one who is cast into the charnel pits; so the grave is among the honors bestowed upon the Muslim. Abu ʿUbaydah said: fa-aqbarahu means He commanded that he be buried. He said: the Banu Tamim said to ʿUmar ibn Hubayrah, when Salih ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman was killed: "Bury Salih for us," and he said: "Take him."

Thumma idha shaʾa ansharahu: He revives him after his death.

Kalla: a response to him, that is, the matter is not as you say, and the view of this disbeliever. Al-Hasan said: decisively.

Lamma yaqdi ma amarahu: he did not do what his Lord commanded him, and did not perform what was obligatory upon him. Fa-l-yanzuri al-insanu ila taʿamihi: how his Lord determined and arranged it, so that it might be a sign and a lesson for him. Mujahid said: to its entrance and its exit.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: al-Qati'i narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from ʿAli ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from al-Dahhak ibn Sufyan al-Kilabi: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "O Dahhak, what is your food?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, meat and milk." He said: "Then to what does it proceed?" He said: "To what you know." He said: "Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, said: He has struck the example of what comes out of the son of Adam as a parable for this world." [93] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/425.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Malik narrated to us, saying: Ibn Hanbal narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahim Abu Yahya narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Yunus, from ʿUbayd, from al-Hasan, from ʿAtiyy, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The food of the son of Adam has been made a parable for this world, and even if it is seasoned and salted, look at what it becomes." [94] [[Qizhah: a spice mix of cumin and coriander placed in pots and containers; said to be tawabil.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Saqlab narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi al-Khasib narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: Sahl ibn ʿAmir narrated to us, saying: ʿUmar ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Ibn al-Walid, who said: I asked Ibn ʿUmar about a man who enters the privy and looks at what comes out of him. He said: The angel comes to him and says: "Look at what you withheld, to what it has become." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/220.]]

Anna: the Kufans read it with a fatha on the alif, intending the repetition of the preposition, its meaning being: "and let him look to how (anna) ..." Others read it with a kasra, as a new sentence.

Sababna al-ma'a sabba: that is, the rain. Thumma shaqqqna al-arda shaqqa: with plants. Fa-anbatna fiha habban wa-ʿinaban wa-qadban: Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Dahhak said: it means fresh clover (al-ruṭbah). The people of Mecca call fodder qaḍib. Tha'lab said: it was so named because it is cut (yuqḍab) every day, that is, cut. Al-Hasan said: qaḍb is fodder.

Wa-zaytunan: the one from which oil is obtained. Wa-nakhlan wa-hada'iqa ghulban: thick trees, whose singular is aghlab; from it the thick-necked is called aghlab. Mujahid said: intertwined. Ibn ʿAbbas: tall. Qatadah: al-ghulb are noble palm trees. ʿIkrimah: large in their middles. Ibn Zayd: large in trunks and necks.

Wa-fakihatan wa-abban: that is, pasture and herbage. Al-Hasan said: it is grass and what animals eat and people do not. Qatadah: as for the fruit, it is for you, and as for the abb, it is for your cattle. Abu Razin: plants. This is supported by what Ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: whatever the earth produced of what people and cattle eat. ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah from him: the abb is fresh fruits. al-Dahhak: it is chaff. ʿIkrimah: fakihah is what people eat, and abb is what animals eat.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid informed us, saying: Dawud ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, from al-ʿAwwam ibn Hawshab, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, that Abu Bakr was asked about His saying: "wa-fakihatan wa-abban," and he said: "What sky would shade me and what earth would carry me if I said in the Book of Allah what I do not know."

Ibn Hamdun informed us, saying: Ibn al-Sharqi informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim ibn Saʿd narrated to us, saying: my father informed us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas ibn Malik, that he heard this verse and then said: "All of this we know, so what is the abb?" Then he threw down a staff he had in his hand and said: "By the Lord of ʿUmar, this is burdensome! And what harm is it to you, O son of Umm ʿUmar, that you do not know what the abb is?" Then he said: "Follow what has been made clear to you of this Book, and leave what is not."

Mata'an lakum: that is, the fruit. Wa-li-an'amikum: that is, the herbage.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 80, verse 33–42:

﴿فَإِذَا جَاءَتِ الصَّاخَّةُ﴾ means the Great Shout, the Blast of the Resurrection. It is called al-Sakhkha because it deafens the ears; that is, it is so loud in reaching the hearing that it nearly deafens them.

﴿يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ الْمَرْءُ مِنْ أَخِيهِ وَأُمِّهِ وَأَبِيهِ وَصَاحِبَتِهِ وَبَنِيهِ﴾ — a person will not turn to any one of them, being preoccupied with himself. It was also said: out of fear of their demands upon him, because of the obligations and wrongs between him and them. And it was said: because he knows that they will neither benefit him nor avail him anything against God.

I heard al-Sulami say: I heard Mansur ibn Abd Allah say: I heard Abd Allah ibn Tahir al-Abhari say concerning this verse: "He flees from them when it becomes clear to him their helplessness and their scant resource, and that the One who possesses the removal of those griefs and anxieties from him is someone else. Had this become clear to him in this world, he would rely on none but his Lord, who is not overcome by anything, and he would attain the breadth of trust in God and find rest in the shade of entrusting all affairs to Him."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Makhlad related to us, saying: Ibn Alawiyya related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Isa related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bishr related to us, saying: a shaykh of ours informed me, from Sa'id ibn Abi Arouba, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, who said: "The first to flee on the Day of Resurrection from his father is Ibrahim, and the first to flee from his mother is Ibrahim, and the first to flee from his son is Nuh, and the first to flee from his brother is Habil son of Adam, and the first to flee from his spouse is Nuh, then Lut," then he recited this verse, ﴿يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ الْمَرْءُ مِنْ أَخِيهِ﴾, and said: "They narrate that this verse was revealed concerning them."

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abdus informed us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Hamdun ibn Khalid related to us, saying: Abu Hanifa Muhammad ibn Amr related to us, saying: my father related to us, saying: Khulayd ibn Da'laj related to us, from Qatada, concerning the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ الْمَرْءُ مِنْ أَخِيهِ﴾, he said: "Habil flees from Qabil; ﴿وَأُمِّهِ وَأَبِيهِ﴾," he said:

"The Prophet ﷺ flees from his mother, and Ibrahim from his father; ﴿وَصَاحِبَتِهِ وَبَنِيهِ﴾," he said: "Lut from his spouse, and Nuh from his son."

﴿لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مِنْهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ شَأْنٌ يُغْنِيهِ﴾ — it preoccupies him, diverting him from the concern of others. Khaffaf said:

"The war of Banu Malik will spare you / from obscenity and ignorance in the assembly."

Al-Farra' said: Some reciters, namely Ibn Muhayson, read (بِعَيْنِهِ) [bi-'aynihi], and this is shadh (irregular).

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz related to us, saying:

Ibn Abi Aws related to us, saying: my father related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ayyash, from Ata' ibn Bashshar, from Sawda, wife of the Prophet ﷺ, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "People will be resurrected barefoot, naked, uncircumcised, the sweat having bridled them and reached the fat of their ears."

I said: "O Messenger of God, alas for our shame! Will we look at one another?" He said: "People will be preoccupied; ﴿لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مِنْهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ شَأْنٌ يُغْنِيهِ﴾" [95] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 10/333.]].

﴿وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ مُسْفِرَةٌ﴾ — bright, radiant, shining; it is said: "asfara al-subh" when the dawn shone forth. ﴿ضَاحِكَةٌ مُسْتَبْشِرَةٌ﴾ — joyful and glad.

Al-Husayn informed us, saying: Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Fami related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Jabbar related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Ma'in related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn al-Ash'ath informed us, from Shamir ibn Atiyya, from Ata', concerning the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ مُسْفِرَةٌ﴾, he said: "From how long they were dusted in the way of God."

﴿وَوُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَلَيْهَا غَبَرَةٌ﴾ — dust. It is mentioned that the beasts which God, the Exalted, turns to dust after judging between them, that dust is turned onto the faces of the disbelievers. ﴿تَرْهَقُهَا قَتَرَةٌ﴾ — darkness, gloom, dejection, and blackness. Ibn Abbas said: "It covers them with humiliation." Ibn Zayd said: "The difference between ghabara and qatara is that qatara is what rises of dust and reaches the sky, while ghabara is what is lower, on the earth." ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ يُصْنَعُ بِهِمْ هَذَا هُمُ الْكَفَرَةُ الْفَجَرَةُ﴾ — "those are the disbelievers, the wicked."
